title: Ancient Trees in France: Cities to Explore
meta_description: France's oldest tree has an actual birth certificate: planted in 1601, before the Mayflower sailed. Six cities mapped, 84 trees.
intro: France's oldest tree has a birth certificate rather than an estimate. The Robinier of Square Rene-Viviani in Paris was planted in 1601 by Jean Robin, herbalist to Henri IV, from seed the naturalist John Tradescant sent from the Appalachians, before the Mayflower sailed and before the genus that now carries Robin's name even existed. That precision runs through France's other oldest trees, most raised from seed by royal gardeners and university botanists rather than found growing wild: a Cedar of Lebanon that legend says crossed the Channel tucked inside a botanist's hat, a plane tree named for the naturalist Buffon who ran the garden that raised it. Six cities are mapped so far, Paris's botanical lineage alongside Lyon's, Nice's, Bordeaux's, Strasbourg's and Toulouse's own plantings, and French ancient trees tend to come with an actual planting year rather than a growth-ring guess, because someone with a reputation to protect wrote the date down.
